summary: Tenant prefix overwrite led to mid-cycle aggregate credit drift and split invoice lines
description: Issue summary: BrightRetail contacted support reporting a mid-cycle reduction in available billing credits and multiple split line items on their latest provisional invoice. The customer says credits allocated at the start of the billing period (reserved buffer + promotional uplift) dropped unexpectedly over 48 hours, and invoice lines show the same hourly window split across two ledger namespaces. Impact: Customer-facing order-processing jobs experienced throttling alerts when their buffer reached zero; revenue-impact monitoring flagged an SLA breach risk. Environment: prod us-west, org-id: org-BR-994, account uses Dedicated reserved capacity with hybrid fallback to hosted in us-west. Observed between 2026-03-08 02:00 UTC and 2026-03-10 11:30 UTC.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Reconcile hourly postbacks for org-BR-994 between 2026-03-08T00:00Z and 2026-03-10T12:00Z. 2) Filter postbacks by tag namespace; note entries with both 'tenant:brightretail' and a transient 'tenant:br-old' prefix. 3) Run billing replayer against the same window to reproduce split invoice lines and credit allocation changes. 4) Compare ledger snapshots pre- and post-2026-03-08T02:00Z for namespace ownership changes.
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: a deploy of the postback-processor introduced a regression that allowed stale tenant prefix headers to override canonical tenant namespace for a subset of postbacks. Evidence: logs from postback-processor pod postback-processor-7f6b show repeated warnings about "prefix_mismatch" and a transient code path that maps legacy prefixes to new tenant IDs. Query of raw postbacks table (postbacks_raw) returned ~4.2k entries with legacy prefix br-old between 2026-03-08T01:55Z and 2026-03-09T05:10Z. Correlation: the ledger rehydration job ran at 2026-03-09T04:00Z and produced an intermediary aggregation that split buffer credits across two namespaces, which the invoicing run interpreted as separate lines. Temporary mitigation applied: blocked the legacy-prefix mapping in the postback-processor and manually requeued ambiguous postbacks into the canonical namespace. Work left: night-run ledger re-aggregation with dedup and canonicalization, and an account-level credit reconciliation to restore BrightRetail's reserved buffer.
